newsitem.title: CROATIA: Holbrooke back in Balkans to speed up peace.
newsitem.headline: Holbrooke back in Balkans to speed up peace.

text.p: Richard Holbrooke, the U.S. envoy who engineered Bosnia's peace agreement in 1995, returned to the country on Wednesday in an attempt to speed up the peace process.

"It's clear to me from what ambassador (Robert) Gelbard told me and from what I've observed, that progress is being made but at much too slow a pace," he told Reuters Television after arriving at Split airport. "We're here to encapsulate what has happened and try to accelerate the process and keep it moving forward."

Holbrooke and Gelbard, the current U.S. envoy to Bosnia, then entered the villa in Split where Croatian President Franjo Tudjman and the chairman of Bosnia's collective presidency, Alija Izetbegovic, were holding talks.

The two leaders met in Split earlier on Wednesday for a summit which had been postponed several times. They were expected to discuss Bosnia's Moslem-Croat Federation which makes up half of the post-war country.
"We're very pleased to start the trip here, in what is after all an effort to strengthen the federation," Holbrooke said.

Gelbard said they had been invited by Tudjman and Izetbegovic to participate in the summit. "What we're interested in is to make sure that the agreements they have reached are fully implemented. We really are concerned that there has been a significant lag in implementation on the part of all the parties."
